title: The Working Life of Wax
paras: In a museum conservation workshop, Mara Silva examines a nineteenth-century anatomical model whose translucent surface offers the first [[intimation|intimation]] of trouble: a cloudy crescent beneath the abdomen. The model depicts the uterus and [[cervix|cervix]], but her immediate concern is chemical rather than medical. Something within the wax has migrated towards its surface, obscuring details once used to train midwives.

Before treatment, Silva consults the maker’s ledger. Between purchases of pigment and a [[bushel|bushel]] of wheat for the workshop kitchen, it records a [[glutinous|glutinous]] adhesive prepared from animal glue. A marginal note calls translucency the wax’s “[[characteristical|characteristical]] virtue”. Such documents reveal what analysis alone cannot: which effects were deliberate, and which alterations would destroy information [[needful|needful]] for understanding the object.

The same workshop supplied theatrical tableaux. One surviving figure lies [[prostrate|prostrate]] beside a statesman’s desk, representing an [[assassinator|assassinator]] captured after a political murder. Elsewhere, a merchant’s jewelled hands advertise [[ostentation|ostentation]], while a barefoot family embodies [[penury|penury]]. These apparently unrelated commissions depended on the same practical expertise: controlling temperature, colouring translucent mixtures, and making inexpensive matter resemble living tissue under unreliable lamplight.

Silva therefore tests a fragment already detached from the anatomical model rather than polishing away the cloudiness. Under magnification, crystalline deposits suggest that components of the original mixture have separated; removing them could merely postpone their return. Her eventual intervention is modest: a cooler case and carefully limited lighting. The achievement is not renewed brilliance, but a slower rate of change.
zh: 在一间博物馆修复工作室里，玛拉·席尔瓦正在检查一件十九世纪的解剖模型。模型半透明的表面初露异样：腹部下方出现了一弯浑浊的月牙形痕迹。模型展示的是子宫与子宫颈，但她眼下关注的是化学问题，而非医学问题。蜡内部的某种物质已向表面迁移，遮蔽了那些曾用于培训助产士的细节。
着手处理之前，席尔瓦查阅了制作者的账簿。在购买颜料和供工作室厨房使用的一蒲式耳小麦的记录之间，账簿记载了一种用动物胶调制的黏稠胶黏剂。页边的一条批注将半透明性称为这种蜡的“典型优点”。这类文献揭示了仅凭分析无法确定的事情：哪些效果是刻意营造的，以及哪些改动会破坏理解这件物品所必需的信息。
同一家工作室还为戏剧性场景制作蜡像。一尊留存至今的人像俯卧在政治家的书桌旁，表现的是一名在政治谋杀后被擒获的暗杀者。另一处，一位商人戴满珠宝的双手彰显着炫耀之意，而一个赤脚的家庭则体现了赤贫。这些看似毫不相关的订单，依赖的却是同一套实用技艺：控制温度，为半透明混合物着色，以及让廉价材料在不稳定的油灯光线下呈现活体组织的质感。
因此，席尔瓦没有将浑浊部分抛光去除，而是检测了一块已经从解剖模型上脱落的碎片。放大观察后，结晶沉积物表明，原始混合物中的成分可能已经分离；将其去除，或许也只能延缓它们再次出现。她最终采取的干预措施很克制：温度更低的展柜，以及严格限制的照明。修复的成就不在于重现光彩，而在于让变化发生得更慢。

q.s: The anatomical model was used to train midwives for more than fifty years.
q.why: 文中说明培训用途，未说明使用年限。

q.s: The theatrical figures and anatomical models depended on the same practical expertise.
q.why: 第三段明确说这些订单依赖同一套技艺。

q.s: Silva polished away the cloudiness before testing the detached fragment.
q.why: 她检测脱落碎片，而非抛光去除浑浊。
